evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Whatever God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it nor taken from it, so that people fear him (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Proverbs collection 15, sources C-F: toughness, oil on the sceptre, the stranger as leader, nothing added to Enlil's temple, the rivers: Saying: the things of Enlil's temple are counted; nothing may be added to what has been counted, and the names of those who do are to be destroyed; Saying: the Tigris is a duck, the Euphrates a goose; Saying: a stranger (gir5) is the leader in a foreign city; Saying: let the herdsman whip the ox, the shepherd slaughter the sheep; where there is no toughness no man can go about his business; Saying: if oil is poured into (or onto) the shaft of a sceptre, no one would know; A school collection of short Sumerian proverbs and sayings, copied as a numbered series on tablets.

Only in A time for everything; eternity in the heart: God has put 'olam (eternity, or the world) in the human heart, yet man cannot find out the work of God from beginning to end; God has made everything beautiful in its time; God seeks what has been driven away (et nirdaf); what is has already been; A time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones; It is God who makes to laugh and to weep, who gives death and life; What has been is what will be; there is nothing new under the sun; God has given humans an evil task ('inyan ra') to be busy with; Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us; For everything there is a season and a time for every matter under heaven (birth and death, planting and uprooting, etc.); What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

בַּעֲצַלְתַּ֖יִם יִמַּ֣ךְ הַמְּקָרֶ֑ה וּבְשִׁפְל֥וּת יָדַ֖יִם יִדְלֹ֥ף הַבָּֽיִת

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Through sloth the roof sinks and through idle hands the house leaks (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Proverbs collection 18: the idler, the talker who got into the palace, the levelling of hills, the lying dream of Agade: Saying: the hills and the depths will be levelled; whenever there is excess, an axe remedies it; Saying: the idleness of a good-for-nothing (a-ḫur-rum) causes losses; hire him and fire him after half a day; Saying: the whirlwind sent to Agade gave Naram-Suen a lying dream (maš2-ĝi6 lul-la) and provided an interpreter; Saying: a slave entrusted with a burial will be negligent; Saying: the quick one hid, the strong one fled, the talker (ka tuku) got into the palace; Saying: your worthiness is the result of chance (ĝiš-šub, the lot); The heights and the hollows will be levelled; Saying: do not pile up the barley; once piled it will be eaten by your lord; Saying: 'Whirlwind, I sent you to Agade: what did you do in Agade?' - 'The dream was favourable'; A spirit volunteers in the divine council to be a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths; The race is not to the swift nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise; time and chance (pega') happen to all; Every valley lifted up, every mountain and hill made low, the crooked made straight for God's coming.

Only in Sayings on folly, rulers and hazards (dead flies, slaves on horses): Do not curse the king even in thought nor the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the air will carry the voice; If the iron is blunt and one does not whet the edge, he must use more strength; wisdom helps one succeed; Dead flies make the perfumer's ointment stink; a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor; The toil of fools wearies them, for they do not even know the way to the city; Bread is made for laughter, wine gladdens life, and money answers everything; He who breaks a wall is bitten by a snake; he who quarries stones is hurt; he who splits logs is endangered; Folly set in high places, the rich sitting low; slaves on horses and princes walking like slaves; If the ruler's anger rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness allays great offenses; The heart of the wise is to his right, the heart of the fool to his left; Woe to the land whose king is a youth and whose princes feast in the morning; happy the land whose king is noble-born; If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer (ba'al hallashon); Wicked compared to a deaf adder that stops its ear against the snake-charmer's spells; and 2 more.

Only in Proverbs collection 19, sources D-H: the um bird, the slave girl's banquet, the fool, the river grave, the insatiable glutton, the early-married youth: Saying: the early-working shepherd, the early-working farmer, the young man who married while young: who compares to them?; Saying: a great river is a grave (ki-maḫ); Saying: from the horizon to the heart of heaven the bread is too little for his great stomach; the grain of the whole land is too little for him; Saying: morsels of bread and tasty onions are the food of the school (e2-dub-ba-a); Saying: the um bird flees, running away from its own behind; Saying: he who keeps fleeing flees from his own past (eĝer, what is behind him); When the lady leaves the house the slave girl comes in from the street and sits at her own banquet; Four things are never satisfied: Sheol, the barren womb, earth not filled with water, and fire that never says 'Enough'; Sayings about the slave girl (geme2): her grumbling, her theft revealed at the mill, her feasting when the mistress is out, her release money; A proverb with frank sexual or scatological content (penis, vulva, anus, breaking wind) used for humour.

Only in One father, one God; foreign wives and the wife of one's youth: The people cover God's altar with tears, weeping and groaning because he no longer accepts their offering; 'I hate sending away (divorce)', says YHWH, and covering one's garment with violence; Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away [contrast between the texts]; One origin (one father, one pair, one God) as ground for conduct toward others [divergence between the texts]; God's attitude to divorce [contrast between the texts]; Whether separation of spouses is allowed or hated by God [contrast between the texts]; 'Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously with one another?'; Marrying foreign women will lead the sons into idolatry; Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away.

Only in Proverbs collection 22, lines 19-101: the husband who picks the fish bones, the younger son driven out, good and evil in the hands, accept your lot: Saying: good is in the hands and evil is also in the hands (a man's deeds are his own); Saying: as the sun rises decisions (destinies) are made; when Utu stands up, kingship is given; Saying: chasing a younger son away from his father's house is an abomination to Ninurta; Saying: a plant as sweet as a husband does not grow in the desert; my husband heaps up for me, my child measures out, my lover picks the bones from the fish; Fable: the pig squeals on its way to slaughter and the butcher tells it that its ancestors and forebears walked the same road; Saying: accept your lot (ĝiš-šub) and make your mother happy; run fast and make your god happy; Saying: collecting firewood is a job for the strong man; the weak man sits waiting for him on dry land; Saying of the servant: with my mouth I cool the hot soup for you, I pick the bones out of the fish for you; Sumerian saying that a listed act is niĝ2-gig, an abomination or taboo, to a named god (Utu, Suen, Ninurta, Inana).

Only in Jephthah son of a harlot recalled from Tob; his historical argument with the king of Ammon: The agreement with the leader is spoken before YHWH at Mizpah; The leader sends messengers to the enemy king arguing from history; An outcast gathers a band of 'empty men' around him; Those who rejected the hero come to him for help in their distress; The son of a harlot becomes a mighty warrior and leader; Israel claims to have held the land for three hundred years; Each nation possesses the land its own god gives it (Chemosh, YHWH); God the Judge is called to judge between two nations.

Only in Proverbs collection 22, lines 203-287: no one reaches heaven, hand at the table, the angry man, the liar, the immigrant, Utu's compassion, the lamentation priest and the lion: Saying: the man seized by anger pours it out in threats (I will glare, I will destroy your wall), and it means nothing; Saying: a god seizes the man who eats (too much); Saying: his hand is on the table, his tongue in the palace; Anecdote: a lamentation priest is afraid of a lion in the desert; the purification priests ask what his brother is doing in the desert; Saying: Utu's glance is prayerful and his heart wide (compassionate); his devotee is holy, and one allotted by Utu for good reaches the quay like a laden ship; Wish: may your friend reach his goal like a ship a good harbour; may your enemy, like flood water, return to his own city; Saying: the liar is arrogant, always lies, always slanders; treacherous, malicious, shifty-eyed; Saying: eating a little does not kill a man, eating modestly is to live well, but coveting (igi-tum3 la2) kills; No one is tall enough to reach the heights (heaven, the mountains) or to span the earth; Saying: when there is a quarrel, the one who has stolen reveals what she took; Saying: he who has silver is happy, he who has grain is comfortable, he who has livestock can sleep; No one is tall enough to reach heaven, or broad enough to span the mountains; and 1 more.

Only in Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing): Do not say 'Why were the former days better than these?', for it is not from wisdom you ask this; The end of a thing is better than its beginning; patience is better than pride; Like the crackling of thorns (sirim) under a pot (sir), so is the laughter of the fool; In the day of prosperity be joyful, in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other; A good name is better than good oil (shem / shemen), and the day of death than the day of birth; Better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; Oppression makes a wise man foolish and a bribe destroys the heart; Vexation is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad; Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?; Wisdom is a shelter (shade) as money is a shelter; wisdom gives life to its possessor; Let them laugh a little and weep much; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; and 1 more.

Only in Hymn to Gilgameš: two-thirds god, eleven cubits tall, the far traveller (Gilgameš SB I): The hero roams the regions of the world searching for (eternal) life; The hero's giant body is measured in cubits (height eleven cubits, chest four cubits, stride six cubits); Gods (the mother goddess and the wise god) design and perfect the hero's body before birth; The culture-hero opens passes through the mountains and digs wells on the hillsides; The hero restores the cult-centres destroyed by the flood and re-establishes the rites for humankind; A far-travelling hero reaches the place where the sun rises; Giants or heroes (Nephilim) born from divine-human unions; The hero is two-thirds god and one-third human; The king is a wild bull, a calf born of a wild cow (the goddess) and reared on butter and milk in the cow-pen; The hero travels to the end of the world and reaches the immortal flood survivor; The king is called a god's son, born of a divine cow, or suckled at a goddess's breast; Formula: there was none like him among all the kings before or after.

Only in Awake, Zion; the feet of the herald: God bares his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations; Because of the exile God's name is continually blasphemed or profaned among the nations; You were sold for nothing and will be redeemed without money; Zion's watchmen sing together, seeing eye to eye YHWH's return to Zion; Zion is told to awake, shake off the dust and put on her beautiful garments; the uncircumcised will no longer enter; Command to the exiles to go out and flee from Babylon, touching nothing unclean; Proclamation among the nations: 'YHWH is king' (YHWH malakh); How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the herald announcing peace and good news: 'Your God reigns'.

Only in Gilgameš oppresses Uruk; the gods hear and Aruru creates Enkidu from clay (Gilgameš SB I): The gods create a rival equal to the overbearing hero, so that they contend and the city may have rest; The oppressed people's complaint about their king reaches the gods, who act on it; A king exhausts the young men of his city with incessant games or labour; The tyrant king lets no girl go free to her bridegroom (claims the bride before the husband); Ishmael foretold to be a wild ass of a man, his hand against all; A wild man, hairy and naked, eats grass with the gazelles and drinks at the water-hole with the herds; A hunter or trapper encounters the wild man at the animals' water-hole and is terrified; A god fashions a creature from clay to serve his purpose; A deity chooses the ruler, 'the true shepherd', in the divine assembly for his attractiveness or worth.

Only in Elihu - warning dreams and the interceding angel: The healed man sings before men, 'I sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not requited to me'; God does all these things two or three times with a man, to bring him back from the Pit to the light of life; God speaks once, even twice, but people do not perceive it; An angel, an intercessor (malakh melits), one among a thousand, declares a man's uprightness and pleads for him; The sick man's soul draws near the Pit and his life to the 'destroyers' (memitim, angels of death); 'Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom (kofer)'; 'The spirit of God has made me, and the breath of Shaddai gives me life'; In dreams during deep sleep God opens people's ears and seals their warning, to turn them from pride and spare them from the Pit; The angel of death (malak al-mawt), put in charge of humans, takes their souls; Angels glorify God and ask forgiveness for those on earth; The restored man's flesh becomes fresher than a child's and he returns to the days of his youth; Humans created from sticky clay (tin lazib); and 4 more.

Only in Ūta-napišti's discourse: the fool's lot, man snapped like a reed, the mayfly, the hidden day of death (Gilgameš SB X): Litany 'at some time we build a house, at some time we start a family, at some time brothers divide, at some time the river floods' on the transience of all things; Saying: no one builds a palace or sets a throne in the council for a fool; he gets dregs instead of ghee, bran instead of flour, rags instead of garments; The great gods and the mother of destinies established death and life, but did not reveal the day of death; Man's name (progeny) is snapped off like a reed in the canebrake; death abducts the comely youth and maiden; Image of human life: the mayfly floating on the flood gazes at the sun and is suddenly gone; No one sees death, sees its face or hears its voice, yet savage death cuts man down; One dies in full prosperity, another in bitterness; both lie alike in the dust covered by worms; Death and life (in that order) are set or created by the divine; Better a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king; one goes from prison to the throne, then is forgotten; Humans are not told the day or the place of their death; The hero's sleepless toil and wandering only fills his sinews with pain and brings his end nearer: what has he achieved?; Saying: I walk about and do not tire, I keep moving and do not sleep; and 2 more.

Only in Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution: Because sentence (pitgam) against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil; There are righteous men who receive what the wicked deserve and wicked who receive what the righteous deserve; Keep the king's command because of the oath of God; who can say to him 'What are you doing?'; I saw the wicked buried with honor, going in and out of the holy place, and praised in the city where they did such things; Who is like the wise and knows the interpretation (pesher) of a thing? Wisdom makes his face shine; Man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it; When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back!; Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Human days on earth are a shadow; Wisdom or the fear of YHWH adds days and years of life; the years of the wicked are shortened; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in Udug-hul compendium (STT 2 173): Namtar and the evil messengers; Ea's remedy of a clay substitute figure taken to the steppe before Šamaš: A bird (dove) of heaven is released and the direction of its flight, toward sunrise or sunset, is taken as an omen; The demons are 'evil messengers' (mārū šipri lemnūtu) who attack the land, fill it like locusts and lay sickness on man; At dawn the substitute figure is carried out to the steppe before the sun god, given provisions in a leather bag and set at the root of a thornbush facing sunset; Closing wish: may the evil demon stand aside and the good protective spirits (šēdu, lamassu) be present; The illness is hidden: no one knows its inside, and its poison cannot be seen; Asalluhi (Marduk) sees the affliction and reports it to his father Ea, who answers 'what I know you know; go, my son' and prescribes the ritual; Namtar, the netherworld deity of fate, 'decrees all the fates'; A gag or affliction keeps food and drink from the sufferer's mouth; The washing water from the speaker's body and hands carries the evil onto a substitute figurine (ṣalam nigsagilê) which bears his sin in his place; street and way undo his sins; Augury: a bird's flight or alighting is an omen bound to a person [divergence between the texts].

Only in Harper's Song of Antef (pHarris 500): generations pass, follow your heart: A song set in the tomb, sung by a harper before the dead owner, on death and how to live; No one comes back from the beyond to tell of the dead and comfort our hearts; The mourners' wailing does not save a man from the underworld; the weary-hearted dead does not hear it; Men build great structures to endure, but the builders and their buildings pass [divergence between the texts]; A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever; The speaker has heard the words of the famous sages Imhotep and Hordedef, yet their own tombs have vanished; Go, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine; let your garments always be white and oil not lack on your head; enjoy life with the woman you love; No one can take his goods with him into death; what he owned falls to others; Generations pass away and others take their place, since the time of the ancestors (or of the god); Refrain 'Make holiday (a beautiful day)! Do not weary of it!'; Even the tombs of those who built great houses have crumbled and vanished, as if they had never been; Follow your heart (desire) while you live: put myrrh on your head, dress in fine linen, do your things on earth.

Only in Namburbi against an ominous sacrifice (STT 2 231): when the slaughtered sheep does not bleed and its entrails are faulty: Wish that the evil cross the river, cross the mountain and be thousands of double-hours from the body, rise like smoke and like an uprooted tamarisk never return; Circling his house, the client declares 'I change my house: my evils are your evils' and tears out the evil the gods placed; Instead of prostrating, the supplicant goes straight to the god's house and kisses its door frame; The client of a ritual is dressed in a strange costume of debasement: grain and silver on the head, jaw bound, rings on fingers and toes, a lead belt, one sandal, wall plaster on the head; The bewitched man calls on the gods of the night (the stars), Night personified and the night watches to hear his case against the witch; Not looking back when leaving behind the doomed place or the banished evil [divergence between the texts]; The god resolves (releases) evil, frightening dreams and bad portents and makes evil and sin pass by; Divination by inspecting the liver (hepatoscopy); The enemies of God vanish like the glory of the pastures, like smoke; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place; A ritual action is performed seven times; A pursued victim raises his hands to the sun god: 'You are a just judge, do not fail me'.

Only in Ašḫella's plague ritual, the rams and the adorned woman sent to the enemy's border (CTH 394 §1-5): Rams, woman, bread and beer are driven through the camp and left on the enemy's border, where our people do not go: 'whoever finds them, may that land take this evil plague'; An adorned woman is set before the king's tent with beer and bread and is driven out with the substitute animals; The plague god is told: these rams are very fat in liver, heart and member; let human flesh be hateful to you, be content with these rams; The officers stretch their hands toward the substitute animals, and bow behind the rams, the king and the adorned woman; In a plague in the army each officer provides a ram; coloured wool and rings are tied on the rams' necks and horns and they are tethered before the tents at night: 'whichever god made this plague, be content with these'; A substitute (animal or person) is given to the deity in place of a human life [divergence between the texts]; Living goat bears the people's sins away into the wilderness.

Only in Šurpu II (SpTU 2 13 obv.): the catalogue of sins - good for evil, bribed judges, the widow wronged, father set against son, captives kept in darkness, false measures: Catalogue sin: he did not release the captive or loosen the bound man, and did not show light to the prisoner; Catalogue sin: he despised father and mother, was hostile to his elder brother and sinned against his elder sister; Catalogue sin: he knew but did not say, said but exaggerated, said 'there is' for 'there is not'; Catalogue sin: he separated son from father, father from son, daughter from mother, daughter-in-law from mother-in-law, brother from brother, friend from friend; The wicked kill the widow, the stranger and the orphan; Whether a bound captive is released or killed; Knowing the matter and not speaking: withholding testimony as a sin; Making the judge take a bribe to win a case; Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, darkness light and bitter sweet; The wicked takes a bribe from the bosom to pervert the ways of justice; Giving with the small measure and taking with the large: short weight to others, full weight for oneself; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

Only in Kummanni prayer, further cases, unknown offences and colophon of Lūrma (CTH 382 §8-13): The storm god filled the mother's breasts for our good, and as people are sated with cold water so may he grant satiety; Since humans know only the words that came out of their mouth, the underworld gods are asked to search out in the dark earth the offences they do not know; If the gods grant the plea, the king will be his god's glory: gods and men will say 'truly the god recognised this man', and his descendants will revere the god; Petition not to be held for offences committed unknowingly, forgotten or by mistake; Plea that the deity not destroy the whole community for what one or a few have done; Intercessor asks: shall one man sin and you rage at the whole community?; A text ends with a note on its source or on where it was written.

Only in House-building ritual (SpTU 2 16 rev.): Kulla escorted to the river bank with provisions and adjured by heaven, earth and the primeval divine pairs never to return: A Sumerian incantation adjures the great storm and evil away with the repeated word 'oath'; The brick god Kulla is installed in a house under construction and, when it is finished, ritually escorted out to the river bank with provisions and forbidden to return; The demons are exorcised by heaven and earth and by the primeval divine pairs (Anu and Antu, Enlil and Ninlil, Duri and Dari, Laḫmu and Laḫamu) and by everyday things (incense, shadow, daylight, path, seat); Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place; The speaker sends sorcery and the evil word away on the wind.

Only in Muršili II's 'second' plague prayer, the causes found (CTH 378.2 §1-10): An offering to a river (the Māla, Euphrates) performed by earlier kings has been neglected since the father's days and is found to be a cause of the plague; The king finds old tablets in the archive which reveal a neglected ritual and a broken treaty as possible causes of the plague; A plague strikes the land because the king's father broke an oath sworn by the gods (by killing the lord to whom he had sworn or by attacking a treaty partner); The Egyptians ask the Hittite king for his son as their king, and when he is sent they kill him; Prisoners of war brought home from the campaign carry a plague into the land; The king offers the gods a restitution (šarnikzel) and reconciliation (maškan) offering for the land's plague, together with his house; The Hittites break the treaty sworn before the storm god with Egypt (the Kuruštamma treaty) by attacking Egyptian territory; The king asks the gods to send the anguish from his heart and take the fear from his body; Confession formula before the god: 'It is so; we have done it'; The king inquires of the gods by oracle and the oracle establishes the hidden cause of the plague; Let an ecstatic come and name the offence, or old women, diviners or augurs name it, or let a man see it in a dream; A plague has raged in the land for twenty years, with great numbers dying; and 2 more.

Only in Lunar eclipse ritual at Uruk: the kalû's lament ('the Dilmunite whose ship sank am I'), the brazier, kispu, mourners with covered heads (BRM 4, 6 obverse): During a lunar eclipse a brazier is lit at the temple gates and the lamentation priest performs laments until the moon becomes bright again; In a lament the god (or his mourner) says: I am the one who roams and does not sleep, who ate no food and drank no water in his weariness; Mourners smear their faces, hands and feet with river mud and hang a dagger at the collarbone; Lament: I am the Dilmunite whose ship sank in the reed thicket; Prayer refrain: may confinement, murder, rebellion and (the evil of) the eclipse not come near the city and its temples; Destruction is ascribed to 'the word of An and the word of Enlil', to the angry heart of the high gods; An eclipse of the moon as a portent of disaster before which people seek escape or protection [divergence between the texts]; A disgraced man goes home mourning with his head covered; A funerary offering (kispu) is made to the netherworld gods (Anunnaki) within a royal rite; After the rite the remains (brazier and ashes, magic circle, twine, purification materials) are thrown into the river; In the ruined temple the offerings, festivals, songs, drums and priestly offices cease.

Only in Priestly instructions for burnt, grain and sin offerings; the perpetual fire: The priest removes the ashes in linen garments and changes clothes to take them out; A garment spattered with sin-offering blood is washed in a holy place; An earthen vessel that held sacred meat is broken; a bronze one is scoured and rinsed; The anointed priest offers a daily griddle-cake grain offering, half morning half evening; A priest's own grain offering is wholly burned and not eaten; A sin offering whose blood is brought inside the sanctuary is burned, not eaten; The remainder of the offering is most holy and eaten by the priests; Section headed 'This is the instruction (torah) of the ... offering'; Whatever touches the most holy altar or holy things becomes holy; Priests wear linen breeches to cover their nakedness, on pain of death.

Only in Šuʾila to Ea: king of wisdom, by whose incantation of life the dead does not die; may my speech please god and king (CTN 4, 167): Prayer that the god loosen the evil bonds tied by sorcerer and sorceress; Prayer: may my speech please god and king; may god and king do what I say; may my mouth and tongue counsel me well; By the wise god's 'incantation of life' the moribund recover and the bonds of witches are released; Closing blessing: may heaven rejoice over the deity, the deep be glad, and all the gods bless and magnify her; God is 'the lifter of my head'; The god brings the river flood and abundance, makes plenty sprout in seas and reed-beds, and creates grain, the life of the people; A prayer is labelled a lifted-hand prayer (šuʾila) and followed by its ritual: roof swept, pure water sprinkled, portable altar, censer of juniper, libation, recitation three times, prostration.

Only in Ea has seen the dead; the gods bellow; battle with the cut-off Ullikummi and his boast (CTH 345.I.3.1 §25-34): A god is distressed at having seen the dead in the dark earth, standing like dust; All the gods assemble and bellow at the monster like cattle; The monster declares he will go up to kingship in heaven, take the city and the holy temples and pour the gods out of heaven; The stone child is set like a spear on the right shoulder of the giant who bears the world (Upelluri), and grows there; The storm god's bulls Šeri(šu) and Tella are fetched, horns anointed, tail gilded, for his battle wagon; The chief god refuses help and the wise god (Enki) grants it; The proud one plans to ascend to heaven, raise his throne above the stars of El and make himself like Elyon; The monster sets up a throne, is named king and judges lawsuits, challenging the god's kingship.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Altars on the roof (the upper chamber of Ahaz) for astral worship (weight 6.8); People bow down to all the host of heaven (weight 6.6). Pair score 13.5.

Only in Uruk nocturnal ritual: offerings on the ziggurat roof to Anu and Antu of heaven and to the seven planets; the great torch; fire carried to every temple and house; gates open till dawn (TCL 6, 41): On the festival night the city watch lights fires in the streets and squares and the city gates stay open until dawn; At nightfall on the temple tower a purification priest lights a great aromatic torch with sulphur fire and recites the hymn 'Star of Anu, lord of heaven'; A large ḫarû jar is broken before the god during the festival rite; On the festival night the gods sit in the temple court in a vigil (bayyātu) until dawn; the gate is not shut; Fire from the temple's great torch is carried down and kindled in every temple of the city, and the people light brushwood fires in their houses; The ritual torch is extinguished in holy water mixed with beer, milk, wine and oil; The king sets out offerings to the planets and stars of heaven and prays to them for long life and a firm throne; The god enters his newly built house in procession and takes possession of it; Water for washing the hands is presented to the gods (mê qātī našû), and the king and the people touch it.

Only in Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah: Men thickened on their lees who say in their hearts 'YHWH will do neither good nor evil'; The Day of YHWH is a sacrifice he has prepared, with invited guests consecrated; Litany of the Day: day of wrath, distress, ruin, darkness, cloud and thick darkness, shofar and alarm; God will search Jerusalem with lamps to find the complacent; Named districts of Jerusalem (Fish Gate, Mishneh/Second Quarter, Maktesh/Mortar) wail; A prophet's genealogy is traced several generations back to a king (Hezekiah); God will punish officials and princes who wear foreign garments; People bow and swear both by YHWH and by Malkam (their king or Milcom); God will sweep away humans, beasts, birds of the air and fish of the sea from the face of the ground (creation reversed); Idolatrous priests (kemarim) who burned incense to Baal, sun, moon, constellations are put down; 'The imminent (al-azifa) has drawn near'; none but God can remove it; Priests do not tread on a temple threshold, explained by an event; and 6 more.

Only in Harper's Song of Neferhotep, third song (TT 50): the good journey and the name not forgotten: Anubis lays his hands on the dead man as the mortuary rites are performed; Those who receive the dead greet him with 'peace' on his arrival [divergence between the texts]; The gods of eternity receive the dead man's ba, protect his mummy and greet him 'welcome in peace'; The good man's name endures in the mouths of later people; The dead official took part in the Osiris rites: dragging the Sokar barque, raising the djed pillar, hoeing the earth at Busiris; The two kites (Isis and Nephthys) sit at the tomb door and lament the dead man's name; The just dead man's name will not be forgotten for ever; he is remembered for his goodness and spoken in people's mouths; The day of death is called the day of 'landing' (mnj), mooring in the land that loves silence.

Only in Job curses the day of his birth: Professional cursers of the day, who are ready to rouse Leviathan, are invoked to curse a day; The dawn imaged as having eyelids; The night personified as announcing 'a man-child is conceived'; 'The thing I greatly feared has come upon me'; God hedges a man in so his way is hidden (inverted image of the protective hedge); The bitter long for death and dig for it more than for hidden treasure; The sufferer curses the day of his birth and the night of his conception; Sufferer wishes he had died in the womb or been a hidden stillborn.

Only in Childless Danel feeds the gods for seven days; Baal intercedes; El blesses him with a son who will do a son's duties (Aqhat 1.17 I-II): A list of a son's duties to his father: setting up the ancestral stele, making his smoke rise, silencing his slanderers, supporting him when drunk, offering for him in the temples, plastering his roof and washing his clothes; Told he will have a son, the father's face shines; he laughs, rests his feet on the footstool and says his soul is at rest; The high god takes a cup in his hand, a goblet in his right, and pronounces a blessing on a mortal; A childless man pleads with the deity for a son to inherit from him and stand in his house, and is granted one; When he kisses his wife she conceives; when he embraces her she becomes pregnant; The promised son is described by his duty to his father (holds his hand, serves him; barr bi-wālidayhi); A ritual action is repeated day by day for six days (one, two, three ... six) and on the seventh comes the result; The son sets up the stele of his father's ancestral god, the emblem of his clan in the sanctuary; A god brings the king's offerings to his father, the high god, and asks him to decree an eternal destiny and long life for the king; A childless king beseeches the god daily for an heir, citing his sacrifices and piety; A person lies down to sleep in a temple in order to receive a dream from the god; The high god El is 'the Bull, your father', 'the Kindly, the Compassionate (lṭpn il dpid)', 'Creator of creatures', 'father of years'.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The son sets up the stele of his father's ancestral god, the emblem of his clan in the sanctuary (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Childless Danel feeds the gods for seven days; Baal intercedes; El blesses him with a son who will do a son's duties (Aqhat 1.17 I-II): A list of a son's duties to his father: setting up the ancestral stele, making his smoke rise, silencing his slanderers, supporting him when drunk, offering for him in the temples, plastering his roof and washing his clothes; Told he will have a son, the father's face shines; he laughs, rests his feet on the footstool and says his soul is at rest; The high god takes a cup in his hand, a goblet in his right, and pronounces a blessing on a mortal; A childless man pleads with the deity for a son to inherit from him and stand in his house, and is granted one; When he kisses his wife she conceives; when he embraces her she becomes pregnant; The promised son is described by his duty to his father (holds his hand, serves him; barr bi-wālidayhi); A ritual action is repeated day by day for six days (one, two, three ... six) and on the seventh comes the result; A good son takes his father by the hand when he is drunk and supports him when he is sated with wine; A god brings the king's offerings to his father, the high god, and asks him to decree an eternal destiny and long life for the king; A childless king beseeches the god daily for an heir, citing his sacrifices and piety; A person lies down to sleep in a temple in order to receive a dream from the god; The high god El is 'the Bull, your father', 'the Kindly, the Compassionate (lṭpn il dpid)', 'Creator of creatures', 'father of years'.

Only in Zakkur stele face A - besieged by Bar-Hadad and sixteen kings, Zakkur lifts his hands and Baalshamayn answers through seers 'Do not fear' (KAI 202 A): A king is besieged by a coalition of many named kings with their armies, who raise a siege wall and dig a moat; The god answers the king's prayer through seers (ḥzyn) and diviners; The king calls himself a humble (or lowly) man whom the god saved and made king; Ben-Hadad son of Hazael king of Aram is named; The king lifts his hands to the god and the god answers him; Hard pressed by a superior enemy, a leader or army calls on God and God answers; A deity made the king king (hmlk-): 'the god made me king'; Oracle of salvation: 'Fear not, for I am with you; I will strengthen and help you'; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision.

Only in Abilum cursed with blindness; seven years of mourning with wailing women; mourning ends with sacrifice (Aqhat 1.19 IV): Mourning is ended: the mourning women are sent away, sacrifice is offered and incense rises to the heavens and the stars; Abilum, 'the city of Prince Yarikh' (the moon god), near the site of the murder; A king in mourning clothes gives up his regalia and persists for seven years; The mountain where the heroes fell is cursed with neither dew nor rain; Mourners shave their heads, clip beards and gash their bodies.

Only in Lament for virgin Israel; seek me and live; the Day of YHWH is darkness: Futility curse: you built houses of hewn stone but will not live in them, planted vineyards but will not drink their wine; The city that marched out a thousand will have a hundred left, and the hundred ten; Dirge: 'Fallen, no more to rise, is the virgin Israel'; God will exile them beyond Damascus; 'I hate, I despise your feasts'; God rejects offerings and the noise of their songs and harps; They hate the one who reproves in the gate and abhor the one who speaks the truth; 'Let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream'; Rhetorical question: did you bring me sacrifices in the wilderness forty years?; The prudent will keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time; Israel carried Sakkuth their king and Kaiwan their images, the star of their god; 'Seek me and live'; do not seek Bethel, Gilgal or Beersheba; Woe to those who desire the Day of YHWH: it is darkness and not light; and 11 more.

'Did I not smite Yamm, beloved of El, River the great god, muzzle Tunnanu, smite the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads ...': The dragon (Tunnanu, Hebrew tannin) is muzzled (ištbm) and destroyed; On seeing messengers arrive the goddess's feet shake, her loins break, her face sweats: 'what enemy has risen against Baal?'; An enemy drove the storm god from the heights of his mountain like a bird from its nest and from the throne of his kingship; God broke the heads of the sea dragons (tanninim) on the waters; 'Am I Sea, or the Dragon (tannin), that you set a guard over me?'; YHWH with his hard, great, strong sword will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and slay the dragon (tannin) in the sea; At bad news or a sudden sight the hearer's feet shake, loins break, face sweats and back gives way; A seven-headed serpent is among the monsters slain by the warrior god; God crushed the heads (plural) of Leviathan, the many-headed sea serpent; A catalogue of monsters the warrior god has already slain (dragon, six-headed ram, Anzu bird, seven-headed snake...); God rides through the heavens (rokhev shamayim) to help.

Only in The Sea's floods rise to the stars; the gods bring tribute to the Sea; Ištar summoned (CTH 346.9): The gods acknowledge the Sea and throw tribute of gems, silver and gold into the water; The sea's floods cover the land and rise up to the sun, moon and stars; Waters rise above the highest mountains (fifteen cubits); A goddess adorns herself, plays instruments and sings by the sea to charm a monster, but it is deaf and blind.

'Did I not smite Yamm, beloved of El, River the great god, muzzle Tunnanu, smite the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads ...': The dragon (Tunnanu, Hebrew tannin) is muzzled (ištbm) and destroyed; On seeing messengers arrive the goddess's feet shake, her loins break, her face sweats: 'what enemy has risen against Baal?'; An enemy drove the storm god from the heights of his mountain like a bird from its nest and from the throne of his kingship; A deity boasts of the monsters already destroyed: Sea beloved of El, River the great god, the dragon (tnn) muzzled, the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads, Arš, the calf ʿAtik, the bitch Fire, Ḏabib; God broke the heads of the sea dragons (tanninim) on the waters; YHWH with his hard, great, strong sword will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and slay the dragon (tannin) in the sea; At bad news or a sudden sight the hearer's feet shake, loins break, face sweats and back gives way; A seven-headed serpent is among the monsters slain by the warrior god; God crushed the heads (plural) of Leviathan, the many-headed sea serpent; A catalogue of monsters the warrior god has already slain (dragon, six-headed ram, Anzu bird, seven-headed snake...); God rides through the heavens (rokhev shamayim) to help.

Only in Job - human life as hard service; 'Am I Sea or Dragon?': Life's days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle; The sufferer's flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; his skin cracks and festers; God called 'watcher of humankind' (notser ha'adam) who targets the sufferer; 'What is man that you make so much of him?' turned into a complaint against divine scrutiny (cf. Ps 8); Sufferer says God will seek him in the morning and he will be no more; Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [divergence between the texts]; Human life on earth is hard service (tsava), its days like those of a hired laborer; God terrifies the sufferer with dreams and visions at night; Like a vanishing cloud, whoever goes down to Sheol does not come up; his place knows him no more; Sea, deep or sea monster subdued or defeated by God.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.4 V: El's grey beard instructs him; let Baal give his rain, his voice in the clouds and his lightning; let a caravan bring silver, gold and lapis; Anat brings the good news; Kothar arrives and sits at Baal's right; 'shall I put a window in the house?' - 'No': A caravan brings silver from the mountains, gold from the hills and gems to build a house of silver, gold and pure lapis lazuli; The craftsman guest is given a throne at the right hand of the storm god and the gods eat and drink; The goddess praises the high god: 'you are great, you are wise; the grey hair of your beard instructs you'; A scribal note within a poem instructs the reciter to go back and repeat an earlier passage; With a house the storm god will give the season of his rain, of snow, his voice in the clouds and his lightning flashes to the earth; A goddess brings good news (bšr): 'rejoice, a house is given you like your brothers'; The craftsman asks twice whether to put a window in the palace; the god refuses ('lest Yamm...'), then later orders it opened; How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the herald announcing peace and good news: 'Your God reigns'; Grey hair is a crown of glory, found in the way of righteousness; At the storm god's roar from the clouds heaven and earth shake, mountains quake and the seas are stirred up; The god instructs the chosen king to build or raise high his temple.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The creatures' wings sound like many waters, like the voice of Shaddai; and 14 more.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.4 VI: 'you will come back to my word'; cedars from Lebanon and Sirion; fire burns in the house six days and on the seventh the silver has become plates and the gold bricks; Baal feasts his brothers, the seventy sons of Athirat: The builders go to Lebanon and its trees, to Sirion and its choice cedars, for the god's palace; Fire burns in the house for six days; on the seventh it dies down and the silver has turned to plates and the gold to bricks; The god celebrates his finished house with a feast for his brothers, the seventy sons of Athirat: rams, ewes, oxen, thrones and jars of wine for gods and goddesses; Fire is kindled to make the bricks of a lofty house or tower [divergence between the texts]; A dwelling built or roofed with silver and gold [divergence between the texts]; A great building work takes six days to complete [divergence between the texts]; Time formula: 'a day, two days passed' (ym wṯn), counted on to the seventh day, or 'days, months, years'; A leader has seventy sons; The craftsman asks twice whether to put a window in the palace; the god refuses ('lest Yamm...'), then later orders it opened; Cedars from Lebanon floated by sea to Joppa for the temple, paid with food and oil to Sidonians and Tyrians.

Only in Fire from heaven, the dedication feast and God's night reply: God appears to the king at night to answer his prayer; God's eyes and heart will be in the temple perpetually; 'If my people who are called by my name humble themselves, pray and turn, I will heal their land'; The people bow with faces to the pavement when the fire and glory descend; God chooses the temple as his 'house of sacrifice'; Dedication (hanukkah) of the altar with gifts after its anointing; The bronze altar is too small, so the middle of the court is consecrated for offerings; Nations ask why God did this to the land and are answered: they forsook the covenant; The king makes the musical instruments used for temple praise; The dynasty's continuance is conditioned on the heirs' faithfulness; Fire comes out from before God and consumes the offering on the altar; Israel becomes a horror, proverb and byword among the nations; and 3 more.

Only in The earth laid waste; the host of heaven imprisoned; YHWH reigns on Zion: The 'city of chaos' (qiryat tohu) is broken; every house shut, joy banished; The earth is polluted under its inhabitants because they transgressed laws and broke the everlasting covenant; a curse devours it; YHWH empties the earth and lays it waste, twisting its surface and scattering its inhabitants: priest as people, master as slave; The earth breaks, splits, totters and reels like a drunkard and sways like a hut; it falls and will not rise; On that day YHWH punishes the host of the height in the height and the kings of the earth, gathering them as prisoners in a pit, shut up and punished after many days; Prophet cries 'razi li, razi li' ('my leanness/my secret is mine'), woe to me, the treacherous deal treacherously; The moon is abashed and the sun ashamed, for YHWH reigns on Mount Zion with glory before his elders; Remnant left like gleanings at the olive-beating: two or three berries at the top of the bough; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; The quake of the Hour: every nursing mother forgets her suckling, every pregnant one miscarries, people seem drunk though not drunk; Whether heaven and earth mourn a destroyed people [contrast between the texts]; 'Terror, pit and snare': who flees the terror falls into the pit, who climbs out is caught in the snare; and 1 more.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.4 VII: Baal takes sixty-six cities; he orders the window opened, a rift in the clouds; he gives his holy voice, the earth quakes, the mountains tremble, his enemies flee to the forests; 'I alone rule the gods'; messengers to Mot: A cedar (spear or lightning bolt) leaps from the storm god's right hand at his foes; At the storm god's voice his enemies grasp the forests, his foes the flanks of the mountain; The god declares: 'I alone rule over the gods, I fatten gods and men, I satisfy the multitudes of the earth'; The god challenges: 'shall any king or non-king establish dominion over the earth?'; The storm god goes from city to city and seizes sixty-six cities, seventy-seven towns; The palace window is opened as a rift in the clouds, through which the god gives his holy voice; The storm god's servants see the sea wrapped in gloom and the highest mountains in darkness; The sole sovereign god is the one who feeds (gods, men, all) [divergence between the texts]; The windows on high are opened and the foundations of the earth shake (flood imagery); The craftsman asks twice whether to put a window in the palace; the god refuses ('lest Yamm...'), then later orders it opened; At the storm god's roar from the clouds heaven and earth shake, mountains quake and the seas are stirred up; At God's coming the earth quakes, heavens drip and mountains flow.

Only in Psalm 29 - the voice of YHWH over the waters: In his temple all say 'Glory!'; The voice of YHWH hews out flames of fire (lightning); The sons of gods (benei elim) are summoned to ascribe glory and strength to YHWH; The voice of YHWH makes the hinds writhe in labor and strips the forests bare; The voice of YHWH shakes the wilderness of Kadesh; The voice of YHWH thunders over the many waters; YHWH sat enthroned over the flood (mabbul); YHWH sits as king forever; The voice of YHWH breaks the cedars of Lebanon and makes Lebanon and Sirion skip like calves and young wild oxen; The thunder glorifies God with his praise, and the angels too in awe of him [divergence between the texts]; God gave David the Psalms (Zabur); Thunder is the roaring voice of God; God's strength for the people like the horns of the wild ox (re'em); and 1 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.5 I: Mot's message: though you smote Lotan the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads, you shall go down into my throat; my appetite is the lion's of the steppe, the whale's in the sea; you did not invite me to the feast: The heavens wither and droop (when the storm god is defeated); The personified underworld speaks of its own unfilled appetite [divergence between the texts]; Death's appetite is that of the lion of the steppe and the whale in the sea, a pool that wild bulls seek; his cup is mixed with a whole river; Death complains that the storm god did not invite him to eat bread and drink wine with his brothers; Leviathan, the great sea monster, named; YHWH with his hard, great, strong sword will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and slay the dragon (tannin) in the sea; A seven-headed serpent is among the monsters slain by the warrior god; Sheol enlarges its appetite and opens its mouth without limit to swallow the people; God crushed the heads (plural) of Leviathan, the many-headed sea serpent; The storm god's mountain Ṣapān is 'my holy place, the mountain of my inheritance, the pleasant place, the hill of victory'.

Only in The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes: Woe to one who makes his neighbor drunk in order to gaze on his nakedness; The prophet stations himself on his watchpost to see what God will answer to his complaint; 'The righteous shall live by his faith (emunah)'; A series of 'woe' (hoy) taunt-sayings against an oppressor; The stone cries out from the wall and the beam answers from the woodwork; The vision is for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come; Write the vision plainly on tablets so that a runner may read it; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; The earth will be full of the knowledge of YHWH as the waters cover the sea; Peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for nothing; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; God asks Gehenna 'Are you full?' and it answers 'Are there any more?'; and 7 more.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.5 V: 'take your clouds, your wind, your rain, your seven lads, your eight boars, Pidray and Tallay, and go down; be counted among those who go down to the earth'; Baal loves a heifer in the field at the shore of death, seventy-seven times; she bears a boy: The storm god is told to take his clouds, wind, rain, his seven lads and eight boars and his daughters, and go down into the earth; The mighty storm god obeys the instruction to go down to death; Instruction: 'be counted among those who go down into the earth', so that the gods will know he is dead; Messengers to the underworld must go to the two mountains at earth's edge, lift the mountain on their hands, and go down into the 'house of freedom'; A storm wind is paired with a seven/eight count; If God is silent the speaker will be like those who go down to the Pit (bor); The storm god's daughters (or brides) are Pidray daughter of light, Tallay daughter of showers (dew), Arṣay daughter of the wide earth.

Only in Elkunirša gives the storm god to Ašertu; Ištar overhears and warns him; purification (CTH 342.1.2): Incantation priests (of Amurru and elsewhere) purify a god from perjury, anger, sacrilege and evil words; A goddess flies like a bird over the desert, finds the endangered god and warns him; A goddess turns into a cup in a god's hand and into a bird (owl) on his wall to overhear husband and wife; The elder god allows his wife to treat the young god as she wishes; The god of dreams himself speaks to the sleeper; Someone learns of a plot against the hero and hurries to warn him.

וְֽיָרְד֞וּ מֵעַ֣ל כִּסְאוֹתָ֗ם כֹּ֚ל נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הַיָּ֔ם וְהֵסִ֨ירוּ֙ אֶת מְעִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֶת בִּגְדֵ֥י רִקְמָתָ֖ם יִפְשֹׁ֑טוּ חֲרָד֤וֹת יִלְבָּ֨שׁוּ֙ עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ יֵשֵׁ֔בוּ וְחָֽרְדוּ֙ לִרְגָעִ֔ים וְשָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלָֽיִךְ

וְנָשְׂא֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ קִינָה֙ וְאָ֣מְרוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵ֣יךְ אָבַ֔דְתְּ נוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת מִיַּמִּ֑ים הָעִ֣יר הַהֻלָּ֗לָה אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיְתָ֨ה חֲזָקָ֤ה בַיָּם֙ הִ֣יא וְיֹשְׁבֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁר נָתְנ֥וּ חִתִּיתָ֖ם לְכָל יוֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Princes of the sea step down from their thrones, strip off embroidered robes, sit on the ground trembling and raise a lament (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.5 VI: the messengers found Baal fallen in the land of the shore of death: 'mighty Baal is dead'; El comes down from throne to footstool to earth, pours dust on his head, gashes cheek and chin, ploughs his chest: 'Baal is dead, what of the peoples?'; Anat roams every mountain: The high god comes down from his throne to the footstool and from the footstool to the ground, pours ashes and dust on his head; The mourner covers himself with a loincloth or sackcloth (mizrt) instead of clothing; Lament: 'Baal is dead! What of the peoples? The son of Dagan! What of the multitudes? After Baal I will go down into the earth'; Gashes in the flesh for the dead and tattoo marks are forbidden; The king rises from his throne, removes his robe, covers himself with sackcloth and sits in ashes; The place where the god fell: 'the pleasant land of pasture, the lovely field of the shore of death (šḥlmmt)'; The mourner gashes cheeks and chin, scores his arms, ploughs his chest like a garden and his back like a valley; Mourners cry 'woe' and throw themselves prostrate in the dust; A goddess roams the streets searching for the captive god: 'where is he held?' and goes to the gate of the grave; Mourners shave their heads, clip beards and gash their bodies.

Only in Oracle on the fall of Tyre and the princes of the sea: God brings up the deep (tehom) over the city and the great waters cover it; God brings many nations against the city as the sea brings up its waves; Nebuchadrezzar, 'king of kings', comes from the north with horses, chariots and siege works; Tyre will be scraped to bare rock, a place for spreading fishing nets in the midst of the sea, never rebuilt; Tyre gloats over Jerusalem: 'Aha, the gate of the peoples is broken; it has turned to me'; God brings the city down with those who descend to the Pit, to the people of old, in the netherworld among ancient ruins; Enemies will descend to the lowest parts of the earth (tahtiyyot ha-arets); Persian ruler styled 'king of kings'; The destroyed one will be sought but never found again; 'I will make you terrors and you shall be no more'; Mockers gloat 'Aha, aha!' (he'ah) over the sufferer; The noise of the city's songs and the sound of its lyres will be heard no more; Oracle or vision dated by year, month and day of the exile of King Jehoiachin.

Only in The king turns against him; seven courtiers conspire; friends, kin and slaves become enemies; goods and offices given to others (Ludlul I 55-104): Whoever spoke well of the sufferer fell into a pit and whoever said 'Mercy on him' died quickly, while his slanderer prospered with a god's help; The sufferer's own slave curses him in the assembly and his slave girl slanders him before the crowd; Brothers, kin, guests, maidservants and servants all estrange themselves from the sufferer; his breath is strange to his wife; The king's heart hardens against his loyal official; courtiers conspire, each vowing to seize his life, post, office or household; The sufferer has no one to walk at his side and sees no champion or helper; The sufferer is pointed at in the street, eyed askance in the palace; his own city glowers at him like an enemy; The man who walked proudly learns to slink; his proud head bends to the ground, his broad chest is pushed aside by a youth; A clique of seven courtiers, one after another, swears to destroy the official and share out his position; The once eloquent sufferer is muzzled as with a snaffle; his lips fall silent, he becomes like a deaf-mute; The fallen man's possessions are shared out among the riffraff, his fields and canals ruined and his offices given to a stranger.

Only in Psalm 38 - the sick penitent abandoned by friends: God's arrows have sunk into the sufferer and his hand pressed down on him; Superscription 'to bring to remembrance' (lehazkir), linked to the memorial offering; Because of his sin the sufferer's wounds stink and fester; no soundness in his flesh; The speaker fasted in sackcloth for his enemies when they were sick; they repay evil for good; Plea: 'Do not rebuke me in your anger nor chasten me in your wrath'; The sinner must confess the sin he committed; Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in A year passes and it worsens; diviners fail; treated like one who neglected the gods though he was pious; the unknowable will of the gods; human fickleness (Ludlul II 1-48): He who lived yesterday died today; in an instant people go from gloom to song, from hunger like corpses to rivalling their gods; The sufferer, who was punctilious in prayer, offerings, festivals and teaching reverence, is treated like one who neglected his god and goddess; Who can learn the reasoning of the gods in heaven's depths or fathom their counsel? Where could humans learn the ways of a god?; A list of the impious man's faults: no libations, no invocation at meals, no prostration, skipped holy days, flour offerings withheld, oaths sworn lightly; The exorcist recoils from the symptoms and cannot diagnose them; the diviner gives no time limit to the illness; The sufferer calls to his god, who does not show his face; he prays to his goddess, who does not raise her head; What is good to oneself may be an offense to a god, and what seems abominable to one's heart may be good to one's god; Protagonist clears himself with a series of conditional self-curses ('If I have done X, may Y befall me'); 'Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?'; Human life is short and fleeting (heled, a handbreadth, grass, a sigh); The king's experts cannot interpret the dream; The god's ingenuity is like tangled threads no eye can follow; he is his own counsellor and no one comprehends his deeds.

Only in Do not be overly righteous; the search for the sum of things; the snaring woman: Be not overly righteous nor overly wise; be not overly wicked nor a fool: hold to both; the God-fearer escapes them all (golden mean); God made humankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes (hishshevonot); Do not take to heart everything people say, lest you hear your servant curse you; you have often cursed others; There is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins; One man in a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find; Qohelet construed once with a feminine verb ('amrah qohelet'); There is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness and a wicked man who prolongs his life in his evil; Wisdom gives the wise more strength than ten rulers in a city; The woman whose heart is snares and nets and whose hands are fetters is more bitter than death; the sinner is caught by her.

Only in Maqlû Ritual Tablet 1-31': the night rite begins — mouth-washing, the tallow figurine on the torch, prostration, Nuska on the roof: A tallow figurine with salt in its mouth is set on a burning torch so that it drips away over a bowl; The speaker raises a reed torch and kindles (sets alight) the fire god himself; May the witch's mouth be tallow and her tongue salt: her evil word drips away like tallow, her witchcraft dissolves like salt; A protective circle (zisurrû) is drawn with flour or gypsum around the burning vessel, the bed or the gates; Incense and offerings are made to the heavenly goddess on the roofs of the houses; A ritual tablet lists the incantations of a series by their opening words, each with the ritual act or material prescribed for it; The victim makes figurines of his witch and warlock and sets them before the gods (or hands them to the fire god) as the accused in his lawsuit.

Only in Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple I - iron tongues, slanders taken, the Ḫantašepa deities (CTH 416 §1-19): Wooden Ḫantašepa deities with blood-stained eyes and blood-red garments hold human heads and spears; Clay cups filled with a liquid (tarlipa-) are carried in and called 'blood'; A basin holds a 'heaven' of iron and one of copper with nine nails; Tongues of iron are put in the mouths of king and queen and the 'tongues' (slanders) of the population are taken from them; King and queen spit three times on a clay figurine, an ox, or a clay army that carries off their evil; After removing the royal couple's evil the expert sacrifices and asks the gods for mercy and protection; A clay army set on a bread, with a bronze dagger on it, is waved over or spat on by the royal couple and then buried; The participants eat and drink at the end of the rite; The carrier figurines and cups are buried in the earth and nailed down so that the evil may not come back up.

Only in Maqlû VII 80-100: 'Huntress of huntresses, witch of witches, whose net is cast in the streets': Curse that named gods kill the witch, erase her name, tear out her tongue and strike her cheek; The witch, 'huntress of huntresses', casts her net in the streets and roams the squares seeking the young men and women of the city; The witch roams the streets, prowls the alleys, spies about the squares and keeps entering houses; The witch is addressed by a string of titles including female cult functionaries (qadištu, nadītu, ištarītu, kulmašītu), ecstatic, exorcist and snake charmer; The evil plan devised against others returns upon the plotter's own head; The witch's spells, bonds and knots are loosed and undone (pašāru, puṭṭuru) and her deeds nullified.

Only in Against the false prophets and the women who hunt souls: False prophets will not be in the council of God's people nor written in the register of the house of Israel; The prophets of Israel are like foxes (jackals) among ruins; Diviners profane God for handfuls of barley and crumbs of bread; False prophets mislead the people saying 'Peace' when there is no peace; The true prophet's task is to go up into the breaches and build a wall for the people on the day of battle; false prophets did not; God tears off the magic bands and lets the trapped souls go free 'like birds' (leporhot); Parable: one who builds on the brink of a crumbling bank falls with it into hell; None more wrong than one who falsely claims revelation or says he can send down the like of God's; Whether a prophet takes payment for his message [contrast between the texts]; False prophets daub a flimsy wall with whitewash (tafel); God's storm, flood-rain and hailstones bring it down; Kings or people practice divination (qesem) and augury (nihush); False prophets prophesy 'from their own heart', following their own spirit, having seen nothing; and 3 more.

Only in Marduk's Address to the Demons 100'-128': 'May Asalluḫi extirpate you' — handed to the gatekeepers of the netherworld; exorcised by heaven and earth: The demons are handed to the gate of the Land of No Return, to the seven gatekeepers of Ereškigal, to Namtar and to the chief gatekeeper, who shuts the gate on them; A speaker adjures or swears 'by the life of heaven'; The evil powers are adjured 'by the life (nīš)' of named gods (Šamaš, Ea, Asalluḫi, Girra) to separate from the speaker; Death himself is driven away, netted and led down to the queen of the netherworld and her gatekeeper; The demons are exorcised by heaven and earth and by the primeval divine pairs (Anu and Antu, Enlil and Ninlil, Duri and Dari, Laḫmu and Laḫamu) and by everyday things (incense, shadow, daylight, path, seat); Exorcistic litany: be off, begone, depart, flee from my body; do not turn back, approach or draw near to my body.

Only in Telipinu myth, the gods under the hawthorn and the anger shut in bronze vessels below (CTH 324.1 §31-37): A magic goddess (Kamrušepa) halts the god's fury and takes from his body his anger, wrath, sin and sullenness; What goes into the place below cannot come out again [divergence between the texts]; The underworld or hell has seven doors or gates; The god's anger, wrath, sin and sullenness are to burn like brushwood, dry like malt, go out like fire, not flow back like water in a pipe; The gods hold assembly under the hatalkešna-tree (hawthorn), where long years lie and all the gods sit; The evil is shut in below under a closed cover; The god's anger must not go into the fruitful field, the garden or the forest, but take the road of the dark earth; The god's anger, wrath, sin and sullenness are sent down to the dark earth into cauldrons of bronze or iron with lids of lead; what goes in does not come up but perishes there.

Only in Syncretistic Hymn to Marduk 18-60: 'Your name is Anšar ... Dagan ... Adad ... Šamaš ... your name is indeed Marduk': Syncretistic litany: each great god (Anšar, Dagan, Adad, Nannar, Šamaš, Erra, Ningirsu) is declared to be a name or aspect of the one supreme god: 'your name is X ... your name is indeed Marduk'; The supreme god alone holds the rope (ṣerretu) or bond of heaven and earth, his sceptre laid across the netherworld; YHWH rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt; Egypt's idols tremble before him; How thunder in the clouds relates to the god: his own roar or a creature praising him [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; Whatever name is pronounced, it belongs to the one god: 'he is our god' / 'his are the beautiful names' [divergence between the texts]; The god is creator of everything, without whom nothing whatsoever was formed and no lord could exist; The god's command cannot be altered and his assent cannot be changed; The god (alone) holds the heavens (and earth) in place: the bond or rope of heaven, holding back the sky; Each line of a litany is repeated for one god under several names (Ninurta, Pabilsaĝ, Ninĝirsu), identifying them; The gods come and prostrate themselves before the victorious warrior god and greet him; The sun god is the king of justice who illuminates the land like a torch and assures the king's just rule; The moon god renews his light, born every month, light of heaven and earth; and 2 more.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.4 VII: Baal takes sixty-six cities; he orders the window opened, a rift in the clouds; he gives his holy voice, the earth quakes, the mountains tremble, his enemies flee to the forests; 'I alone rule the gods'; messengers to Mot: A cedar (spear or lightning bolt) leaps from the storm god's right hand at his foes; At the storm god's voice his enemies grasp the forests, his foes the flanks of the mountain; The god declares: 'I alone rule over the gods, I fatten gods and men, I satisfy the multitudes of the earth'; The god challenges: 'shall any king or non-king establish dominion over the earth?'; The storm god goes from city to city and seizes sixty-six cities, seventy-seven towns; The palace window is opened as a rift in the clouds, through which the god gives his holy voice; The storm god's servants see the sea wrapped in gloom and the highest mountains in darkness; Sevenfold refrain 'the voice of YHWH' (qol YHWH) as thunder over waters, cedars, fire, desert; The sole sovereign god is the one who feeds (gods, men, all) [divergence between the texts]; The windows on high are opened and the foundations of the earth shake (flood imagery); The craftsman asks twice whether to put a window in the palace; the god refuses ('lest Yamm...'), then later orders it opened.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The Nile dries up, reeds wither, fishermen mourn and flax-workers and weavers despair (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Neferti laments the coming ruin of land and cosmos (Neferti 20-38/2): Since everything made is as if never made, the creator (Re) is urged to begin the creation over again; Desert (or foreign) animals drink at the rivers of Egypt with no one to drive them off; A strange bird breeds in the Delta marshes, having built its nest beside the people, who let it approach; The land is utterly destroyed; no remnant is left, not even the black of a fingernail; The land is ruined, yet no one cares, no one speaks, no one weeps for it; The prophet addresses his own heart, bidding it stir and weep for the land in which it began; The sun is veiled by cloud and no longer shines, so that people cannot see or live; Cosmic disorder: the south wind blows against the north wind and the sky no longer has a single wind; Asiatics (aamu) come down into Egypt, terrify the harvesters and seize the plough-teams; fortresses are breached; Refrain of the seer: 'I show you the land in sickness' (or 'I show you the son as foe...'), introducing each list of woes; The sun is covered (wrapped) and gives no light; Stars and constellations (kesilim) give no light, the sun is dark at its rising and the moon does not shine.

Only in Oracle on Egypt; the drying Nile; an altar to YHWH in Egypt; 'Blessed be Egypt my people': An altar to YHWH in the midst of Egypt and a standing stone (matsevah) at its border; God stirs up Egyptian against Egyptian, city against city, kingdom against kingdom; A highway from Egypt to Assyria; 'Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance'; When Egypt cries out because of oppressors God sends them a savior; Egypt knows YHWH and offers sacrifice; Egypt consults its idols, the 'ittim (mutterers), ghosts and familiar spirits; Five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear to YHWH; one called 'City of the Sun/Destruction' (ir ha-heres); God mixes a spirit of distortion in Egypt so it staggers like a drunkard in his vomit; The wise counselors of Pharaoh in Zoan and Memphis are fools: 'I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings'; YHWH rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt; Egypt's idols tremble before him; God cuts off head and tail, palm-branch and reed: the elder is the head, the lying prophet the tail; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; Oracle headed 'massa' (burden) against a named nation or place.

Only in Sayings on the fool (the 'book of fools'): Like snow in summer or rain at harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool; He who sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks violence; A proverb (mashal) in the mouth of fools is like lame legs or a thorn in a drunkard's hand; Giving honor to a fool is like binding a stone in a sling; Like a fluttering sparrow or a flying swallow, a curse without cause does not alight; As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly; A rod is for the back of the fool (the senseless).
